description:
Limassol’s Water Museum occupies the former pumping station on Franklin Roosevelt Avenue. The preserved industrial building connects the museum with the development of the city’s water supply.

Historic machinery, water meters, testing equipment and archaeological material introduce different ways of obtaining and managing water. The displays combine technical history with the importance of water in everyday life.

description:
XeniArtSpace is a private art foundation with exhibition spaces in the Trilogy development in Limassol. Its programme connects an international collection with modern and contemporary artistic practice.

Works associated with different twentieth- and twenty-first-century movements are presented alongside temporary projects and Cypriot art. Exhibitions and collection activities offer different ways to encounter the foundation’s artistic interests.

description:
The Zivania Museum occupies a traditional house in Vasa Koilaniou. Its collection explores the production and local use of the Cypriot grape spirit.

Distilling equipment, storage vessels and agricultural objects connect the displays with village work and household traditions. Community donations helped preserve material associated with this aspect of local heritage.
